clinicalPearls: A rare autosomal recessive disorder combining sensorineural hearing loss in both sexes with primary ovarian insufficiency in 46,XX females
Affected males have normal gonadal function, so the ovarian component is not apparent, and the diagnosis may be missed in isolated male cases
Hearing loss is usually bilateral and progressive, ranging from mild to profound
Females may present with primary or secondary amenorrhoea, absent puberty, or premature ovarian insufficiency
Some subtypes include a progressive neurological phenotype with ataxia and peripheral neuropathy
Several genes are implicated, many encoding proteins involved in mitochondrial function and protein quality control, such as CLPP, HARS2, LARS2, and C10orf2 (TWNK)
Management is multidisciplinary, combining audiological rehabilitation with endocrine and fertility care
reference.pathophysiology: Perrault syndrome is genetically heterogeneous, but many of the implicated genes encode proteins critical to mitochondrial function, including mitochondrial aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases and components of mitochondrial protein quality control and DNA maintenance. Impaired mitochondrial protein synthesis and homeostasis particularly affects tissues with high metabolic demand, so cochlear hair cells and the developing ovary are vulnerable, producing progressive sensorineural hearing loss and accelerated loss of ovarian follicles leading to ovarian dysgenesis or premature insufficiency. In neurological subtypes the same metabolic vulnerability extends to the cerebellum and peripheral nerves, adding ataxia and neuropathy.
additionalDifferentials: Turner syndrome and other causes of gonadal dysgenesis
Other mitochondrial disorders with hearing loss
Usher and Pendred syndromes when systemic features overlap
additionalInvestigations: Pure-tone audiometry to characterise and monitor sensorineural loss
Karyotype to exclude Turner syndrome and confirm 46,XX status in females
Endocrine assessment including gonadotrophins and ovarian reserve markers with pelvic imaging
Molecular genetic testing of Perrault-associated genes such as CLPP, HARS2, LARS2, and TWNK
Neurological evaluation and nerve conduction studies where ataxia or neuropathy is suspected
Cross-sectional temporal bone imaging before cochlear implantation when indicated
redFlags: Primary or premature ovarian insufficiency in a young female with hearing loss
Progressive neurological decline with ataxia or neuropathy
Profound progressive hearing loss limiting communication
Fertility and bone-health consequences of untreated ovarian insufficiency
reference.prognosis: Hearing loss tends to progress and is rehabilitated with amplification or cochlear implantation, while ovarian insufficiency usually causes infertility and requires hormone replacement; neurological subtypes carry a more guarded outlook.
pitfalls: Diagnosing isolated hearing loss in a female without evaluating ovarian function
Missing the syndrome in affected males who lack a gonadal phenotype
Overlooking the neurological subtype and its long-term implications
Not arranging early endocrine care to protect bone and address fertility
management: Supportive multisystem care, as no disease-specific drug therapy exists
Hearing rehabilitation with hearing aids and cochlear implantation for progressive sensorineural hearing loss
Oestrogen and progesterone hormone replacement for ovarian insufficiency to induce or maintain puberty and protect bone health
Fertility counselling with assisted reproduction or oocyte donation as appropriate
Neurological management and physiotherapy for the ataxia and peripheral neuropathy of the neurological subtypes
Genetic counselling and family screening for the autosomal recessive genes such as CLPP, HARS2, LARS2 and TWNK
Coordinate audiology, reproductive endocrinology, clinical genetics and neurology input
